sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Cheboygan County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the County Clerk/Register of Deeds office in the county building at 870 South Main Street, Room 204, Cheboygan, MI 49721. The mailing address is PO Box 70, and the main number is 231-627-8808. In Cheboygan County the clerk and the register of deeds are the same office, so the same counter handles court filings, marriage licenses and land records.

The Register of Deeds window is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., a half hour later start than the rest of the clerk's office. The county closes on a fixed list of holidays that includes Good Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, so a closing planned near those dates needs an earlier recording plan.

sections.h2: What is the Cheboygan County Register of Deeds responsible for?
sections.html:
It keeps the official record of real property in the county. The office page says any document that affects real property is recorded there, and it lists warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, wills, mortgages and divorces as examples.

For a seller, that means the register of deeds is where the title chain continues after your sale. The county website also offers recording packets: a general recording requirements sheet, a warranty deed with recording requirements, a land contract form and a quit claim deed with recording requirements. Download those before you ask a title company or attorney to draft, because they show the layout the office expects.

  • Payment is accepted by cash, check and debit or credit card.
  • Coins above $5.00 are not accepted.
  • Card payments can be taken by phone for most services.

sections.h2: How much is the recording fee in Cheboygan County?
sections.html:
State law sets the standard fee at $30.00 for entering and recording a document, regardless of the number of pages. MCL 600.2567 adds $3.00 for each additional instrument when one document assigns or discharges several, $1.00 per page for copies and $5.00 to certify a recorded document.

A charter county may set its own schedule by ordinance, so ask the Cheboygan office to confirm the total before you write the check. The statute also says the fee is due when the document is left for recording, with limited exceptions for electronic filings and government agencies. A short call to 231-627-8808 settles the exact amount.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will I owe on a Cheboygan County sale?
sections.html:
Expect the county and state taxes to be calculated on the full sale price, rounded up in $500 steps. The county rate is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state rate is $3.75 per $500 under MCL 207.525.

Combined county and state transfer tax at sample prices, worked from the statutory rates

The middle row uses $192,500, the Census median value for owner-occupied homes in Cheboygan County for 2020 to 2024. The deed has to state the total value on its face, or carry an affidavit of value. If a sale includes personal property such as a boat or furniture, listing the real and personal values separately keeps the tax on the real property alone.

sections.h2: Which deeds need a tax certificate in Cheboygan County?
sections.html:
Deeds that carry warranty promises need county treasurer certification before the register of deeds will record them. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that taxes on the parcel are paid for the five years before the deed date, along with a statement of any tax liens or titles.

A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is exempt under subsection (6)(e) of that section, and so is a sheriff's deed from a court proceeding. If a deed is presented after March 1 and before the local treasurer has filed the current delinquent tax return, the certificate carries a note that the return was not available, and the register of deeds may not refuse the deed for that reason alone.

sections.h2: What formatting mistakes get a Cheboygan County deed rejected?
sections.html:
The common ones are mismatched names, missing addresses and unreadable signature blocks. MCL 565.201 sets the rules every Michigan register of deeds must apply.

  • Each signer's name is printed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the name in the acknowledgment.
  • A notary's name is printed or stamped on the same page near the notary signature.
  • Every grantee's address appears on the deed, using the street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The name and business address of the person who drafted the deed appears on it.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed or obscured.

A deed in another language needs a written English translation attached. A rejected deed goes back to your attorney or title company for repair.

sections.h2: What should a Cheboygan County seller know about the local housing picture?
sections.html:
Cheboygan County is a large, lightly settled county with a long list of seasonal homes. It covers 885 square miles in total, of which 715 are land and 170 are water, and the Census Bureau puts density at 35.8 people per square mile.

The 2025 population estimate is 25,793, and 30.6% of residents are 65 or older. Owners occupy 85.6% of homes. Median gross rent is $773, and the median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $62,875. The 2020 count found 36.0% of the 17,631 housing units vacant, and the Census lists 74 building permits for 2025. County government was organized in 1853 after a merger with the former Wyandot County.

sections.h2: How do I protect my Cheboygan County property from deed fraud?
sections.html:
Sign up for Property Activity Alert, a service that watches for recordings under your name. The office explains that it cannot stop fraud, but the alert warns an owner early so they can act. Call 231-627-8866 and the staff will enter your name and email address.

This is useful for sellers who keep another parcel in the county, and for anyone who inherited land and has not yet recorded a transfer into their own name.

faqs.q: What are the Cheboygan County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds window runs Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The rest of the clerk's office opens at 8:00 a.m. The office closes on listed county holidays, including Good Friday and the day after Thanksgiving.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees by card in Cheboygan County?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts cash, check and debit or credit cards, and it can take card payments by phone for most services. It does not accept coins over $5.00.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed taxed differently in Cheboygan County?
faqs.a: A quitclaim deed does not need the treasurer's tax certificate, but transfer tax can still apply if money changes hands. MCL 207.505 exempts deeds that only confirm a title already held, and deeds with consideration under $100.

faqs.q: How is the county transfer tax calculated in Cheboygan County?
faqs.a: Divide the sale price by $500, round up, and multiply by $0.55. The state tax uses the same rounding at $3.75. On a $200,000 sale that is 400 units, or $220 county tax and $1,500 state tax.

faqs.q: Does the Cheboygan office help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. Hire an attorney or a title company to draft it. The county posts a general recording requirements sheet and sample warranty and quit claim deed layouts that show what the register of deeds expects.
